title: Local ZTF calibration retains a 0.16 mag optical change in the dust-dimmer candidate G1713
abstract: We test the long optical change of Gaia DR3 1712982358083435520 with new local calibration of ZTF DR24. Ensembles of 41 g and 46 r comparison stars retain a 2021-2022 minus 2023-2024 contrast of 0.158 mag in both bands. A 30-day block bootstrap gives 95 percent intervals of 0.091-0.205 and 0.094-0.216 mag. Removing one comparison star changes either result by less than 0.001 mag. Extra image-fit quality cuts retain the result. On 357 nights with both bands, the colour change is consistent with zero. Seven published NEOWISE visits give a W2 response of 0.362 mag per r mag, with visit-bootstrap interval 0.133-0.516 and positive slope after every single-visit deletion. The exact two-sided rank probability is 0.00675. The g-based W2 relation is weaker. The target and epochs were selected from a prior report, so probabilities are descriptive. These data support optical dimming after local calibration but do not identify a grain size, age or dust source. Code, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and a retrieval recipe are included.
